verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents Runbooks as its automation engine. Runbooks evaluate conditions whenever an incident is declared and then automatically execute actions such as creating Slack channels, starting Zoom meetings or sending webhooks, while Alert Rules and AI summaries also fire without manual intervention. However, the documented automations are event-triggered within the incident lifecycle rather than general-purpose background jobs, so coverage of the story is incomplete. Missing for 10: time-based or recurring scheduled automations, autonomous AI-agent-driven workflows beyond incident-triggered steps, and independent or hands-on corroboration that automations run reliably unattended.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Runbooks are FireHydrant's automation engine. They define and automate a workflow of steps and actions according to specified conditions.
Any time an incident is declared, Runbooks evaluate their conditions to decide whether or not they should trigger.
Automate manual tasks such as creating incident Slack channels, Jira tickets, meeting bridges, and more
Summaries are created as soon as an incident is declared, providing key information right from the start.
Integrate with alerting and monitoring integrations to automatically create incidents from alerts
